validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE: real, independently regulated FERC project, not a GEM-only entity. FERC's own order in Docket CP20-21-000 (172 FERC P 61,073, issued 2020-10-15, https://www.ferc.gov/sites/default/files/2020-10/cp20-21-000.pdf) formally defines the 'Amendment Project' as relocating the previously-approved compressor station from Allen Parish (MP 96.2) to a new site 14 miles west at MP 72.3 in Beauregard Parish ('Beauregard Parish Compressor Station'), and increasing its design horsepower from 89,900 hp to 93,880 hp (four Solar Titan 130E units), plus adding three new interconnects (Cameron Interstate Pipeline, Transcontinental Gas Pipe Line, LA Storage). A follow-on amendment, Docket CP23-513-000 (filed 2023-07-14; Federal Register notices 2023-10-13 and EA availability 2024-02-08), made 38 additional route/construction-method modifications to the same facilities. EIA's Natural Gas Pipeline Projects workbook independently tracks this exact bundle as one line item ('Louisiana Connector Amendment Project', operator 'Port Arthur Pipeline LLC', Docket/Permit Number 'CP20-21 / CP23-513-000 (amendment, 2023)', Cost $88.897M, Miles 0, Additional Capacity 70 MMcf/d, Year In Service 2027) -- confirming GEM's row is tracking a real, correctly-scoped FERC amendment docket family, not a duplicate or a misfiled placeholder. CLASSIFICATION: 'transmission' is correct -- this is an NGA Section 7(c) FERC-jurisdictional interstate facility (EIA's own 'Pipeline Type' field records 'Interstate'; the FERC order is issued under the same certificate authority, Docket CP18-7, as the mainline Louisiana Connector), not a gathering/lateral line. DUPLICATE: checked against the full Port Arthur family on this same gem.wiki page -- P0241 (Louisiana Connector, the 72-mile/42-inch mainline itself) and P3198 (Texas Connector, the separate 31-mile Orange County TX lateral to Port Arthur LNG Phase 2, EIA Docket CP17-21/CP24-512) are both swept separately in batch A3; P3590 (Louisiana Connector Extension, PF19-6-000, shelved) is staged separately within this same batch. P3197 is distinct from all three: it is specifically the compressor-station relocation/upgrade amendment (CP20-21 + CP23-513), never a length of new pipe, which is exactly why LengthKnown=0/Diameter=blank on this row is correct (see spec note below) rather than a sign of a misclassified or duplicate row. ATTRIBUTION: Owner1/Operator = 'Port Arthur Pipeline, LLC' is confirmed as both the FERC certificate holder/applicant in CP20-21-000 and EIA's recorded 'Pipeline Operator Name' -- correct, no relabeling needed.

This is independently corroborated by at least three separate trade-press outlets that did their own reporting rather than merely re-syndicating the release: Oil & Gas Journal ('Sempra Infrastructure places Port Arthur Pipeline Louisiana Connector online'), Engineering News-Record ('$1B Louisiana-to-Texas Gas Pipeline Reaches Finish'), and constructionfront.com (2026-06-10). EIA's workbook (row 'Louisiana Connector- Port Arthur Pipeline', last updated 2026-07-06) records Status='Part Completed', Cost $1,207M, Miles 77, Additional Capacity 2,000 MMcf/d, Diameter 42in, Docket/Permit Numbers CP18-7 / CP20-21 / CP23-513, and a note that 'a portion was approved for in service by FERC 5/29/26' -- consistent with, and slightly predating, the full 2026-06-09 in-service announcement.

EIA's workbook (row 'Texas Connector-Port Arthur Pipeline') records this as a separate 31-mile, 42-inch intrastate lateral from a new Orangefield Compressor Station in Orange County, TX to the proposed Port Arthur LNG Phase 2 facility in Jefferson County, TX -- FERC Docket CP17-21 (original, April 2019) plus CP24-512 (amendment approved June 2025) -- targeting Phase 2 FID in 2025 and construction beginning Q2 2026, distinct from and not to be confused with P3197's Beauregard Parish compressor-station amendment.
